description.narrative:
Stöd till UN Women Strategiska Plan för Bosnien-Hercegovina 2019-2022
Det föreslagna UN Women programmet och dess "concept note" (konceptpapper) begär stöd till UN Women Strategiska Plan för implementering i Bosnia och Hercegovina under perioden 2019-2022. Det föreslagna programmet innehåller fem huvudsakliga resultatområden vilka är följande: i) Styrande strukturer/regelverk samt sektorprioriteringar som reflekterar jämställdhet mellan könen, ii) Kvinnor har inkomstsäkerhet, goda arbetsförhållanden och ekonomisk autonomi, iii) Kvinnor och flickor kan leva ett liv utan våld av olika former, iv) Fred och säkerhet och humanitära överväganden skapade av och för kvinnor samt v) Att förbättra UN Systemet i syfte att bli mer effektivt och koordinerat (strategiska samarbeten).

Support to UN Women Strategic Note in Bosnia and Hercegovina 2019-2022
The proposed UN Women programme concept note requests support for support to UN Women Strategic Note Implementation in Bosnia and Hercegovina during 2019-2022. The proposed programme five main impact areas as follows: i) Governance structures and sector priorities reflect gender equality, ii) Women have income security, decent work and economic autonomy, iii) Women and girls live a life free of violence, iv) Peace and Security and humanitarian action shaped by women and v) To enhance UN System and become more effective and coordinated (strategic partnerships).

The overall goal of the intervention is to contribute to the implementation of UN Women Bosnia and Hercegovina Strategic Note during the period 2019-2023 (the agreement has been extended one year), which encompassess two strategic cycles; Strategic Note 2015-2020 and the Strategic Note 2021-2025.
The Strategic Note 2015-2020 included five so called impact areas:
Impact 1: Governance structures and sector priorities reflect gender equality concerns and committments. Impact 2: Women have income security, decent work and economic autonomy. Impact 3: Women and girls live a life free of violence. Impact 4: Peace and security and humanitarian action are shaped by women leadership and participation. Impact 5: To drive more effective and efficient UN System coordination and strategic partnership on gender equality and women's empowerment.
In the strategic note 2021-2025, there are three overarching thematic areas with impacts and connected outcomes:
1. Women's economic empowerment Impact: Women have income security, decent work and economic autonomy Outcome: By 2025, people benefit from resilient, inclusive and sustainable growth ensured by the convergence of economic development and management of environment and cultural resources Output objectives are: - Governments have improved capacities to promote employment policies that enhance womne's access to decent work and promote income security - Women owned businesses and women entrepreneurs have strengthened capacities and resilience - Women and girls benefit from employment opportunities and education/exchange programs in tech-driven industries
2. Ending violence against women Impact: All women and girls live a life free from all forms of violence Outcome: People have access to better quality and inclusive health and social protection systems Output objectives are: - Legislators and institutions have capacities to incorporate the highest level of international standards on EVAW in legislation, policies and budgets - Women, girls, men and boys at community and individual level are able to mobilze actors, resources and capacities to create an environment for zero tolerance to violence. - General and specialist service providers have improved capacities to deliver quality, accessible and survivor-centered services.
3. Gender responsive governance Impact: Women lead, participate in and benefit equally from governance systems Outcome: By 2025, people contribute to, and benefit from more accountable and transparent governance systems that deliver quality public services, and ensure rule of law. Output objectives are: - Relevant institutions in BiH have increased capacities which ensures that gender responsive policy making, budgeting and integration of EU gender equality and women's empowerment commitments are implemented across sectors - Selected government and political institutions in BiH have increased capacities to ensure the necessary regulatory and procedural preconditions for increased political participation of women - Government institutions and selected CSOs have increased capacities to implement BiH GAP, AP on implementation of UNSCR 1325 and CEDAW Concluding recommendations. - Government and CSOs strengthen multi-stakeholder dialogues
The impact/outcome areas are the same as in UN Women global strategic note as well as the UNSDCF for BiH. Women, peace and security is mainstreamed throughout the programme, where women participation and inclusion in decision making processes is targeted under all areas, notably under gender responsive governance.
Apart from the three programmatic areas and the cruss-cutting areas, the strategic note also includes objectives for organisational effectiveness and efficiency, including UN Women's coordination role within the UN, engagement of partners, communication, internal learning, and internal management and control. Output objectives are: - UN Women effectively leads, coordinates, and promotes accountability for the imlementation of gender euality commitments in United Nations Country Team in BiH. - Effective partnership between UN Women and civil society, and with regional international organizations and gender mechanisms in the country - Effective communication in support to promotion of gender equality and women's rights in the country.

sector.narrative: Women’s rights organisations and movements, and government institutions

description.narrative:
Ending violence against women Regarding the program area ending violence against women, a strategic review indicated that UN Women has played a central role in addressing violence against women in BiH since its establishment. UN Women has evolved from a potential competitor with CSOs to a crucial partner and technical leader in this field. The governments, especially the Gender Centers, have gained important capacity through collaborating with UN Women. CSOs also value UN Women's support to information and service access through one stop shops. The report further notes that UN Women can have an important role in advocating for more sustainable support and funding to specialised services from the governments. UN Women notes from this strategic review, that it has to be more present in the field to improve the visibility, connections with beneficiaries, and to strengthen monitoring and evaluation.
As an example, the system for protection from violence against women was strengthened at national and local levels. 25 multisectoral teams have been supported which has led to strengthened multisecotral teams for protection of survivors/victims of violence against women. In RS, a protocol on handling cases of domestic violence has been signed by six ministries. In FBiH, the Ministry of Interior has endorsed a new standardized approach to the police response to violence against women and domestic violence cases. Through support from UN Women, civil society organizations have contributed to development of draft amendments of legislations (they have been supported to do research based advocacy for enhancement of legislative framework for protection from sexual violence). Through support from UN Women, the Safe Network (CSO's running safe houses in BiH) now has access to a database for keeping records of specialized support services for victims of violence, and thereby the network is better equipped to respond to sexual violence and other forms of genderbased violence.
Efforts to prevent violence against women have taken place in BiH. As an example, six local communities now apply the "Communities that Care" approach, involving youth, men and boys, community members, and nontraditional leaders in preventive activities. Among other things, 24 religious leaders, including members of local interreligious councils have enhanced capacities to conduct prevention activities within their religious communities. Banja Luka city has applied the global UN Women Safe Cities and Safe Public Spaces program focused on combating sexual harassment in public spaces. Furthermore, UN Women's work with local media and multisectoral teams in ten local communities has contributed to indepth media reporting/articles around violence against women, to raise awareness around the violence against women and available protection mechanisms.
Work with Roma women and violence against women has led to that 171 Roma women and girls from four communities in BiH (Tuzla, Kakanj, Prnjavor and Vukosavlje) have better access to their rights, as a result of CSO Bolja Buducnosts and UN Womens support. As a result of advocacy and capacity building efforts two key policy documents were revised: BiH Action Plan for the social inclusion of Roma men and Roma women (20212025), and Action Plan for the inclusion of Roma men and women in Tuzla (20232026). The documents are for the firsttime gender sensitive, reflect the needs of Roma women and include the genderbased violence in Roma communities. Five Roma women's organizations and five activists, members of the Roma women network are empowered and able to influence local and national policies related to Roma rights.
Women's Economic Empowerment Work focused on supporting individuals in different ways. Through different interventions, a total of 250 women in tech-driven industries increased their capacities and skills, for instance on employment and self-employment, cryptocurrencies and digital assets. 15 selected women-owned businesses increased business performance by at least 50 % as a result of a mentoring program that UN Women has supported. Policy-related work has also been carried out, resulting in a study on care economy that will be published soon, a mapping of the entrepreneurial ecosystem in BiH, and a feasibility study on women-owned businesses' access to finance. UN Women has also worked on gender mainstreaming of internal documents in private sector companies, (Women's Empowerment Principles), leading to that five companies updated their personnel policy and/or code of conduct.
Gender Responsive Governance Through programs as well as the normative and coordination mandates including advocacy, promoting accountability for implementation of gender equality commitments, advisory work, exchanges, strategic guidance, analyses, trainings UN Women has worked to improve gender responsive governance in BiH (gender responsive programming and budgeting, implementation of national and international normative commitments, EU-accession). UN Women claims that capacity within targeted institutions has increased in terms of gender-responsive policy making, budgeting and integration of EU gender equality commitments. Results in the past period within gender-responsive budgeting (within the Sida-funded regional project) shows that more government institutions implement gender responsive policy making and budgeting, notable from annual budget allocations to gender equality in BiH (1,45 % at the national level, 5,79 % in FBiH, 6,39 % in RS). Work on gender statistics has improved, where UN Women has supported the development of the Gender Equality Index in BiH. There is now a partial index, which is comparable to gender equality indexes in other European countries. The partial index for BiH will continue to be built on. During 2022, the updated statistical resource Women and Men in BiH 2021 was also produced. Following a recommendation from the CEDAW committee, UN Women has assisted domestic stakeholders on national and entity levels, in consultation with civil society organisations, to develop a framework monitoring system/tool for the implementation to key international and normative standards related to gender equality. This systematic overview and framework of all indicators and data sets needed for different types of international reporting has simplified the reporting procedures as well as provided information to the development of national policies, such as the BiH Gender Action Plan and the 1325 Action Plan.
Coordination and communication Within the UN country team, UN Women has facilitated a comprehensive assessment internally about the System Wide Assessment of Progress (SWAP) related to gender equality. The work has led to increased knowledge about the gender equality marker within programming of UN. UN Women's work to coordinate gender equality work within the UN country team has also led to improved UN policies and programming in terms of gender mainstreaming. Three knowledge products with policy recommendations were produced (focus on gender).
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
